## Three things to remember
:::

- Frames come from the timeline.
- Each scene keeps its own length.
- Presets are data, not code.
:::

::: {.scene component="bullets" duration="3s" animation="slide-up"}
::: {.heading}
## Next steps
:::

- Write the outline.
- Pick the theme.
- Check the fonts.
- Render a draft.
:::

::: {.scene component="bullets" duration="3s" animation="reveal"}
::: {.heading}
## Why it matters
:::

- Points appear in the order written.
- A compact list keeps the slide readable.
- Long points wrap inside the safe area.
:::

::: {.scene component="bullets" duration="3s"}
- A long point that runs over more than one line so that the wrap inside the safe area is checked at the full frame width.
- A second long point, also written as one sentence, to check the line length against the bullet column.
- A third point that is shorter.
- A fourth point with a little more text than the others, so the rows differ in height.
- A fifth point, which should still sit inside the frame.
- The sixth and last point, shown on the final frame of the video.
:::

::: {.scene component="bullets" duration="3s"}
::: {.heading}
## Two points
:::

- One.
- Two.
:::
